title: Non-coding genetic variants underlying higher prostate cancer risk in men of African ancestry.
authors: Li, Shan; Fatema, Kaniz; Sundarraj, Nidharshan; Singh, Arashdeep; Rajagopal, Padma Sheila; Notani, Dimple; Takeda, David Y; Hannenhalli, Sridhar
one_liner_zh: 该文用深度学习模型预测前列腺癌增强子中非编码SNP对转录因子结合的影响，虽聚焦疾病风险而非TF-DNA机制建模，但涉及TF结合位点预测且方法可迁移至TF-DNA互作研究。
abstract: Prostate cancer (PrCa) incidence and severity vary across ancestries; men of African ancestry (AA) are more likely to be diagnosed and die from PrCa than those of European ancestry (EA). Current polygenic risk scores, even from multi-ancestry GWAS, do not fully capture population-specific genetic mechanisms, especially those mediated by non-coding regulatory single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). Using a deep learning model of prostate enhancers, we identify ~ 2000 SNPs, potentially affecting enhancer function, with higher alternate allele frequency in AA men, that may affect PrCa risk. These SNPs may promote cancer via two mechanisms: increased enhancer activity leading to immune suppression and telomere elongation or decreased activity causing de-differentiation and apoptosis inhibition. Identified SNPs predominantly modulate binding of key transcription factors such as FOX, HOX, and AR - the first was experimentally validated. Incorporating these SNPs into a polygenic risk score improves PrCa risk assessment beyond existing GWAS-identified variants.
abstract_zh: 前列腺癌（PrCa）的发病率和严重程度在不同祖先群体间存在差异；非洲裔（AA）男性相较于欧洲裔（EA）男性更易被诊断出PrCa并因此死亡。当前的多基因风险评分，即使基于多祖先全基因组关联研究（GWAS），也未能完全捕捉群体特异的遗传机制，尤其是那些由非编码调控性单核苷酸多态性（SNPs）介导的机制。利用前列腺增强子的深度学习模型，我们识别出约2000个可能影响增强子功能的SNPs，这些SNPs在AA男性中具有较高的替代等位基因频率，并可能影响PrCa风险。这些SNPs可能通过两种机制促进癌症：增强子活性增加导致免疫抑制和端粒延长，或活性降低引起去分化和凋亡抑制。识别的SNPs主要调节关键转录因子如FOX、HOX和AR的结合——其中前者已通过实验验证。将这些SNPs纳入多基因风险评分，可超越现有GWAS识别的变异，改善PrCa风险评估。
